name: Sarah
overview: Sarah, originally named Sarai, was the wife of Abraham and was barren, having no children (Genesis 11:29-30). She accompanied Abraham on his journey to Canaan, demonstrating her close kinship and partnership with him (Genesis 12:5). During a famine, Abraham sojourned in Egypt, and Sarah's barrenness led her to give her handmaid Hagar to Abraham as a concubine, which caused tension as Hagar conceived and Sarah felt despised (Genesis 12:10; 16:1, 4). These passages reveal Sarah's significant role in God's unfolding plan through Abraham, marked by human struggle and divine promise.
